newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Coffee seen still in range despite rise.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Coffee seen still in range despite rise.

text.p: MAY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Coffee looks set to open unchanged to slightly higher after its rises Wednesday, which were inspired by news of smaller than expected U.S. green coffee stocks, traders said.
Analysts did not yet feel that London coffee futures had broken out of their range.

Sucden analyst Adrian Haylor put the trading range on benchmark May at $1,500 to $1,670, "and $1,668 in particular", he said. He noted that the move still left May below its 40-day moving average of $1,624.
"I wouldn't get longer-term bullish until $1,668 is broken," Haylor said.
"Although it was a strong move higher, it doesn't suggest London is out of its range and about to race higher," Haylor said of Wednesday's rise.
"Support looks well established," he said, putting initial support at $1,600 and then on down to $1,529.
The market would face resistance at $1,650, then at $1,668 and on to $1,700.

New York coffee futures charged higher Wednesday, with spot May ending at more than a two-and-a-half-year high as speculators bought heavily after a monthly report showed a much lower than expected rise in consumer coffee stocks, traders said.
Traders' nerves were rattled by news of possible disruptions to supplies in Columbia and Brazil.
A strike by Colombian truck drivers was set to begin at midnight Saturday and looked certain to deepen near-term supply concerns.
Brazil's two key coffee ports after Santos were expected to be hit by a 48-hour national strike by stevedores due to begin at 1000 GMT Friday, unions said.
Union officials in Rio de Janeiro and Vitoria said they were going to take part in the national strike, the second in two weeks following a 24-hour stoppage on April 4.
"A 48-hour strike is definitely more serious than a 24-hour one. Without doubt, coffee shipments will be hit," said Jose Adilson Perreira, president of the Vitoria stevedores union.

Brazil's Espirito Santo state should produce 3.38 million 60-kg bags of coffee in 1997/98, down from a previous estimate of 3.59 million bags published in December, according to the state agricultural secretariat.
